notes: The entire reader brief v12, C.tex, H.tex, C_alerts.md, PREAMBLE.tex, source_paths.json and all 228 lines of the frozen notation snapshot were read before the first image. A truncated first text-tool response was supplemented with complete sequential reads of the snapshot before images.

Coverage: the whole image was opened once for layout, then half_a and half_b once each in order. Every text block, word, ending, accent, abbreviation, punctuation mark, quotation, visible correction and insertion, and every inline/display mathematical expression was compared against both witnesses, including their agreed readings. The single-crop pass covered the places left open; no whole/half image was revisited and no settled place was recropped.

Fourteen open loci were recorded in open_loci.json before any crop was created. Each received one tight crop from the whole-source image, 2400 pixels wide using PIL LANCZOS, autocontrast and UnsharpMask. Each crop was inspected once. Crop boxes, actual processing and UTC image-open records are preserved here and in view_log.json. The initial brief read occurred before the first clock observation; start_utc is the first observed UTC clock value rather than an invented earlier start time.

The sheet is entirely handwritten in one principal dark-pen hand whose personal identity is not established by this packet. The lower-left archive number 14 is lighter and is recorded separately. There is no visible author page number, title, date, salutation, signature, address or written page count on this sheet. No independent diagram or drawing is present.

The two ordinary hooked connectors are insertion signs: (de cochaines) attaches between complexe and tronqué, and par (G,N) attaches after the clipped adjective before est. They are represented with inserted at those attachment points; they are not independent drawings. H's description of the second connector is credited and is not treated as a doubt flag.

The page states that Gr-champs on X épinglés by G,N form a 2-catégorie and even a strict Picard 2-catégorie through the Baer operation, and assigns them the displayed truncated shifted relative derived-section complex. Its NB says that the unshifted relative complex begins in degree 1. These are source assertions, not independently proved conclusions in this run.

The geometric passage describes a relation with 2-gerbes on B_G linked by N and equipped with a trivialisation over the written X approximately B_c=(B_G)_{/P}, then identifies P as an object associated with a universal torsor under G. The final sentence calls the 2-gerbes a 3-catégorie de Picard a priori and stops at mais il se. No continuation was read or supplied.

The crop of the low subscript resolves c by its open shape and absence of an interior e-bar; no expected mathematical interpretation was used to choose the letter. The degree 1, displayed shift [1], truncation relation and later 3 were checked visually only. No proof, independent re-proof, mathematical computation, formal certificate or re-use requiring a mathematical verification was performed, so math_checks is empty.

For the clipped adjective after sur X, the first alternative reproduces only the extant épi-g. No final l/é strokes survive. The fuller alternatives remain doubtful and are not silently supplied. The first catégorie similarly has an i-dot at the edge but no independently visible final e. The other clipped word doubts are retained where a terminal trace survives without secure separate letters.

Three isolated dark points and the small crossed/star-like upper mark are represented without assigning them semantic roles. A phantom alternative concerns textual status, not denial that a physical point exists. The point below J and the point below final de retain their lower positions; the small crossed mark remains above the o of objet.

Differences settled directly in a half carry approximate whole-source pixel boxes in their scan_shows fields so the main reader can make the required adjudication crops without requesting or reopening this reader's views. Ordinary H macro renaming, the archive-number metadata, and the mere absence of a generic handwritten wrapper in H are not counted as differences.
